m.s: Rinse {rice} until the water runs clear. Put it in a saucepan with 1½ times its volume of cold water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes so it finishes steaming.

Pop {beef_rump} in the freezer for 20 minutes so it firms up and slices thin, then slice it across the grain into thin strips. Thinly slice {springonion}, keeping the whites and greens separate. In a bowl mix {soy}, {brownsugar}, {sesameoil}, finely grated {garlic} and {ginger}, and the spring onion whites. Toss the beef through and leave it for 15 minutes.
Thinly slice {cucumber} and toss with {ricevinegar} and a pinch each of salt and sugar. In a small bowl stir {gochujang} into {mayo}, then loosen with a splash of water until it drizzles.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat until it's just smoking. Lift the beef out of the marinade with tongs and cook it in small batches for 1 to 2 minutes each, so it chars rather than stews. Crowd the pan and it goes grey, so take your time.
Put all the beef back in the pan, pour in the leftover marinade and let it bubble for 1 minute until glossy and sticky. Take it off the heat.
Fluff the rice with a fork and divide between bowls. Top with the beef, pickled cucumber and {kimchi}. Drizzle with the gochujang mayo and finish with the spring onion greens and {sesameseeds}.

l: Pack the beef and rice together, with the pickles, kimchi and mayo in a separate container so nothing goes soggy. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
g: Tamari instead of soy, and sriracha mayo instead of gochujang (most gochujang contains wheat). Kimchi usually is GF but check the label. Marinate the GF beef in its own bowl and cook it first.
